info.title: Markitai service API
info.version: set from the build when served
info.summary: Convert files and URLs to Markdown, manage saved jobs and model settings.
info.description: The REST API of `markitai serve`. By default every API client, including loopback clients, sends the startup token as `Authorization: Bearer` (preferred) or `?token=`. Anonymous access in the security alternatives applies only when started with `--no-auth`; settings and URL conversion then remain restricted to direct loopback peers without forwarding headers. An admin may create user tokens (`/api/access-tokens`): a user token admits every route except the settings and the token routes (403 `settings_forbidden`), and its holder sees only the jobs it created (any other job is 404 `job_not_found`). Designated downloads can use a single-use ticket. Every error body is `{detail, code, reason}`; present text by `reason`, then `code`. See docs/serve.md, docs/service-settings.md and docs/provider-management.md for the contracts this document summarizes.

servers.description: The service that serves this document

get.summary: Version, effective model configuration, presets and limits
The conversion options the workbench's composer starts from
get.description: For every caller. `server`: the server's defaults, read from its running configuration (`config.json` over the built-in defaults): `llm` `llm.enabled`, `ocr` `ocr.enabled`, `alt` `image.alt_enabled`, `desc` `image.desc_enabled`, `screenshot` `screenshot.enabled`, `screenshot_only` `screenshot.screenshot_only`, `pure` `llm.pure`, `no_cache` `cache.no_cache`, `no_compress` not `image.compress`, `profile` `output.profile` (null = default output), `strategy` `fetch.strategy` (a server set to `cloudflare` reads `auto`: Cloudflare is never a default). `own`: a user token's own defaults (null otherwise); `defaults`: `own` over `server`. `scope`: where a save goes (`server` for the admin, `user` for a user token); `can_save`: false for an anonymous caller. `revision`: `sha256:` + hex over what a save replaces. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

put.summary: Save the composer's choices as the defaults
put.description: Body exactly `{expected_revision, defaults}` (else 422 `invalid_convert_defaults`). `defaults`: an object of the option names above (only those; each of its type; `strategy` one of auto, static, playwright, defuddle, jina; `profile` rag, obsidian, okf or null), else 422 `invalid_convert_defaults`. The admin writes the options sent into `config.json` at the keys above (a null profile removes `output.profile`) and into the running configuration; `defaults: null` from the admin: 422. A user token replaces its own (`null`: none, the server's apply again), kept in its file under `serve/user-models/`. Stale `expected_revision`: 409 with `detail` `{code: "stale_revision", current_revision}`. An anonymous caller: 403 `settings_forbidden`. Answers as GET. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

get.summary: This OpenAPI 3.1 document, with the build's version

post.summary: Issue a single-use, 60-second ticket for one download
post.description: For clients that must let the browser open a download natively (a navigation cannot send `Authorization`). The returned `url` carries `?ticket=` instead of the token; it admits exactly one GET of exactly `path` within `expires_in` seconds. A ticket presented for another path or method, or a second time, is refused with 401 `ticket_invalid`. At most 64 tickets are outstanding (429 `too_many_tickets`); a body over 8 KiB is refused with 413 `request_too_large`.

post.summary: Replace the access token; other tabs and devices must sign in again
post.description: Trusted like the settings: the current token is required (403 `settings_forbidden` otherwise), and a server started with `--no-auth` has no token to replace (409 `token_disabled`). The body is empty or `{}`. Generates a new 64-character token, replaces the old one at once (it is refused with 401 from then on), revokes every outstanding download ticket and ends every open event stream. The token lives in memory only: a restart takes `MARKITAI_SERVE_TOKEN` or a fresh random token again. User tokens are kept. Admin only: a user token is refused with 403 `settings_forbidden`. The answer carries `Cache-Control: no-store`.

get.summary: The user tokens, oldest first, without the tokens themselves
get.description: Admin only (a user token: 403 `settings_forbidden`); a server started with `--no-auth` has no tokens (409 `token_disabled`). `last_used_at` is kept in memory only: null after a restart until the token is used. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

post.summary: Create a user token; the only answer that ever carries it
post.description: Body exactly `{"label": string}` (else 422 `invalid_json`; over 1 KiB: 413 `request_too_large`). The label is trimmed and must be 1 to 60 characters without control characters (422 `invalid_label`). At most 50 tokens (409 `token_limit`). The token is `mku_` and 64 lowercase hex characters; the server keeps only its SHA-256 (in `MARKITAI_HOME/serve/access.json`), so it survives restarts and admin-token regeneration. A file that cannot be saved: 500 `settings_io_failed`, nothing changes. Admin only; `--no-auth`: 409 `token_disabled`. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

delete.summary: Revoke a user token at once
delete.description: From then on the token's requests are 401 `token_required`, its outstanding download tickets are refused and its open event streams end (every stream ends and reconnects with its own token). Its jobs stay, visible to admins only. Unknown id: 404 `token_not_found`. Admin only; `--no-auth`: 409 `token_disabled`. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The token's id (`u_` and 12 hex characters)

post.summary: Start a job from uploaded files and/or URLs
post.description: Files precede URLs in the returned order. URL conversion requires the token by default; with --no-auth it requires a direct loopback peer without forwarding headers. A request that itself asks for model processing while no model is routable is refused with 422 `llm_unavailable` before anything is stored.

files.description: Repeated file fields; at most 100 MiB each

urls.description: A JSON array of http(s) URLs

label.description: What the submission is called in the history list (a folder or `.urls` file name): plain text without control characters, at most 120 characters after trimming; blank means none. Otherwise 422 `invalid_label`.

urls.description: A JSON array of http(s) URLs

get.summary: The job's current snapshot
get.description: A saved job is kept for `limits.history_retention_days` (7) days after it finished; after that every job route answers 404 `job_not_found`, before the startup or hourly sweep deletes its folder.

get.summary: Server-sent events: a first snapshot, then item and job events
get.description: `event: snapshot` carries a JobSnapshot, `event: item` an Item, `event: job` a JobProgress; a terminal job event ends the stream. Idle keepalives are `:ping` comments every 15 seconds. A slow subscriber receives a fresh snapshot after an event-buffer overrun. Send the token as `Authorization: Bearer` (a fetch-based reader can; the browser's EventSource cannot).

post.summary: Stop the job's original items that still wait for a conversion slot
Queue a retry or an LLM enhancement of one terminal item

delete.summary: Delete one item, its upload and the files it owns; the last item deletes the job

get.summary: The item's Markdown (at most 64 MiB) and its downloadable files
get.description: With `max_bytes`, `markdown` is the start of the document: at most that many bytes, never cut inside a UTF-8 sequence, and ending at a line break when one falls in the excerpt's last quarter. `artifacts` is complete either way. An excerpt of an indexed item reads only its first bytes, so it is also served when the whole document exceeds 64 MiB.

parameters.name: max_bytes
parameters.description: Return at most this many bytes of Markdown; an integer of at least 1024, otherwise 422 `invalid_max_bytes`

get.summary: The item's document JSON (schema version 1): source, properties, Markdown, plain text, pages, images, tables, notices, usage
get.description: v1.19. The same document `markitai --format json` writes; see docs/json-output.md and docs/schema/document-v1.schema.json. Kept when the item finishes and replaced by a retry that publishes a new result. 404 `result_unavailable` when the item has no document: not finished, failed, or converted by a build that did not keep documents.

get.summary: One of the item's own extracted images, inline
get.description: For showing the images of the item's Markdown. Served only when `relpath` is one of this item's result `artifacts` (its asset index; for an older history without one, the assets its Markdown references), names a png, jpg/jpeg, gif, webp or avif file (by extension, case-insensitive; never SVG, Markdown or other files), and resolves to a regular file inside the job output without traversal, an absolute path, a backslash or a symbolic link. Anything else, including an item that is not done, is 404 `file_not_found` (`job_not_found` and `item_not_found` for those); nothing outside the job folder is read and nothing external is fetched. A download ticket cannot name this path. Responses carry the type by extension, `Content-Disposition: inline`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox`, `Cache-Control: private, no-cache` and a weak ETag from the file's size and modification time (answered with 304).

parameters.name: relpath
parameters.description: The artifact's `relpath` exactly as the item's result lists it, relative to the job output and percent-encoded one `/`-separated segment at a time (for example `.markitai/assets/%E5%9B%BE%201%20(a).png`).

ETag.description: Weak validator from the file's size and modification time

get.summary: Download one item's result files and its kept original as a ZIP
get.description: Holds every file the item's result lists in `artifacts`, at those relpaths, and the item's kept original (the upload, or a URL item's page snapshot: the bytes `…/original/file` sends) at `original/<the file name that route sends>`. Sent as `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename*=UTF-8''<item output base name>.zip` with `nosniff`. 404 `job_not_found`, `item_not_found`, or `result_unavailable` when the item has no result; 409 `item_busy` while the item runs or waits for a retry; 413 `archive_too_large` past the job archive's limit. Its path may be named by a download ticket.

get.summary: What the Compare view can show of the item's source
get.description: Chooses, in order: a kept upload of a PDF (`pdf`), of a raster image (`image`: png, jpeg, gif, webp, avif, bmp, tiff, heic/heif), of HTML (`html`) or of a text format (`text`: md, markdown, txt, csv, tsv, json, xml, yaml, yml, log); a URL item's kept page snapshot (`html`); the item's page screenshots, else a URL item's compare screenshots (`screenshots`); otherwise `none` with a `reason`. Page boxes come from the PDF's pages or the image headers (HEIF and AVIF are decoded); no page is drawn. Every original response carries `Content-Disposition: attachment`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox; default-src 'none'`.

get.summary: The stored original bytes: the kept upload, or a URL item's page snapshot
get.description: Sent as an attachment with the original's media type, except that HTML and SVG are sent as `text/plain; charset=utf-8`, so a direct visit never renders them; also `nosniff` and `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox; default-src 'none'`. 404 `original_unavailable` when nothing is kept. Its path may be named by a download ticket.

get.summary: A kept HTML original, for a sandboxed frame of the workbench
get.description: Only for `html` originals (404 `original_unavailable` otherwise); over 10 MiB: 413 `result_too_large`. The stored bytes as UTF-8 text with one insertion right after the first `<head>` start tag, else after the first `<html>` start tag, else at the start after a leading doctype: `<meta http-equiv="x-dns-prefetch-control" content="off">` and `<base href="<the item's URL>" target="_blank">` for a URL item (`<base target="_blank">` for an upload). Sent with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-same-origin allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox; default-src 'none'; img-src https: data:; style-src https: 'unsafe-inline'; font-src https: data:; media-src https:; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-DNS-Prefetch-Control: off`, `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Content-Disposition: inline`: the frame keeps the service's origin (so the workbench can read the page it shows), but no script runs (no `allow-scripts`, no `script-src`: `default-src 'none'` refuses every script, inline handler and `javascript:` URL), no form is sent, and only the site's pictures, style sheets, fonts and media are fetched, over HTTPS. A frame cannot send `Authorization`, so its path may be named by a download ticket.

get.summary: Where the item's screenshots show its page's blocks
get.description: Kept when a browser took the page's screenshots (the conversion's own, else its compare screenshots), read in the page as they were taken; the descriptor's `blocks` names this path when the item has them and its `pages` are those screenshots. The screenshots are the page cut from its top, in `pages` order, covering `width` × `height` CSS pixels; a screenshot `w` pixels wide shows `w / width` pixels per CSS pixel. Sent as `application/json` with `Cache-Control: no-store` and the headers of every original response. 404 `original_unavailable` when none are kept.

get.summary: One page of the original as an image
get.description: `pdf`: page `n` drawn on white, `width` pixels wide (narrower when the 32-megapixel limit requires). `image` (`n` = 1): the stored image when browsers show its type (png, jpeg, gif, webp, avif, bmp) and it is not wider than `width`, otherwise a PNG scaled to `width`. `screenshots`, or `html` for a URL item whose conversion also saved page screenshots: screenshot `n` (the conversion's own screenshots, else the item's compare screenshots), scaled to a PNG when wider than `width`. At most two pages are drawn at a time; another request is refused with 429 `render_busy` and `Retry-After`. Responses carry `Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400` and an ETag (answered with 304), and drawn pages are kept briefly in memory.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Image width in pixels, clamped to 160–2400; 1200 when omitted. Not a whole number: 422 `invalid_page_request`.

get.summary: A PDF page's text as positioned lines, and its pictures' boxes
get.description: Only for `pdf` originals (404 `original_unavailable` otherwise). Text runs on one baseline that follow each other within an em form a line, so a table row may be several lines, one per cell. Lines are in reading order, at most 5000, with boxes in points from the page's top-left corner. `images` lists the boxes the page's pictures are drawn in (same frame, drawing order, at most 500, clipped to the page; none under 4 points on a side). Drawn under the same two-at-a-time limit as page images (429 `render_busy`).

get.summary: A PDF's own outline (bookmarks) as titles, pages and levels
get.description: Only for `pdf` originals (404 `original_unavailable` otherwise). The bookmarks in the outline's order (a parent before its children), each with its title on one line (PDFDocEncoding, UTF-16 or UTF-8 decoded; control characters and white space runs as one space; trimmed; at most 300 characters), the 1-based page it opens and its 1-based level (top-level entries are 1). An entry whose destination is not a page of this document opens the page of the next entry that has one, and is left out when none follows. At most 2000 entries; `truncated` says more exist. `items` is empty when the PDF has no outline or it cannot be read. Read under the same two-at-a-time limit as page images, waited for rather than refused.

get.summary: Download one output file as an attachment

parameters.name: relpath
parameters.description: The artifact's path relative to the job output; it may span several `/`-separated segments. Traversal, absolute paths and symlinks are refused.

get.summary: Download every output file of a finished job as a ZIP
Saved jobs, newest first, including jobs other local processes added
get.description: A user token lists only the jobs it created. Only finished jobs within their retention: a job is deleted 7 days after its `finished_at` (or, without one, its folder's modification time), at server start and hourly; running jobs and jobs with queued retries are never expired.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: `items` adds each job's `options` and its full item list, as the job snapshot shows them, to its entry. Other values are ignored.

get.summary: Download every completed saved job as one ZIP
get.description: A user token gets only the jobs it created; none: 404 `history_empty`.

post.summary: Delete several saved jobs and items in one request
post.description: Body `{jobs?: string[], items?: {job_id, item_id}[]}` with exactly those keys and 1 to 1000 entries in all (else 422 `invalid_delete_request`); not `application/json`: 422 `json_required`; not JSON: 422 `invalid_json`; over 256 KiB: 413 `request_too_large`. Each entry is handled on its own, in order (`jobs`, then `items`), exactly as `DELETE /api/history/{job_id}` and `DELETE /api/jobs/{job_id}/items/{item_id}` handle it (deleting a job's last item deletes the job); a job the caller may not see is `job_not_found`. Deleting is final: there is no rollback of the entries that succeeded. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

delete.summary: Delete a terminal saved job and its files

get.summary: Revision and secret-free saved and detected deployments
Environment, common and saved provider cards

parameters.name: refresh
parameters.description: Accepted for compatibility; the list is computed on every request

get.summary: The editable fields of one saved connection; the key only masked

200.description: Stored fields; the API key is never returned, only masked (an `env:NAME` reference stays unresolved)

post.summary: Add one deployment (compatible with the legacy single-model form)

put.summary: Change the one deployment of an unambiguous routing group

delete.summary: Delete the one deployment of an unambiguous routing group

post.summary: Atomically add up to 50 deployments and remove saved ones
post.description: One change, all or nothing: `remove` lists saved deployment ids and `deployments` the new ones (at least one of the two non-empty). Every id (to remove, and an addition's `credential_deployment_id`) names a deployment of the list `expected_revision` identifies, before this change, so removing the model a provider card stands for and adding another through that card is valid; removals apply first. An unknown id: 404 `settings_entry_missing`; an id listed twice: 422 `invalid_settings_request`; a weight that is not a whole number from 0 to 100: 422 `invalid_weight`; nothing is saved. `SettingsView.batch_remove: true` says the route takes `remove`.

patch.summary: Change one deployment by its stable identity
patch.description: `share` (`private` or `shared`, alone or with the other fields; any other value: 422 `invalid_settings_request`) decides whether users' conversions may use this model: `shared` saves `model_info.share: "shared"` in the configuration file, `private` removes it. It applies to users' next conversion; a shared model with weight 0 is off for everyone.

delete.summary: Delete one deployment; its connection stays saved

patch.summary: Change a saved connection and every deployment linked to it

delete.summary: Delete a saved connection and its deployments

post.summary: Ask the server host's system opener to open the configuration file

get.summary: The configuration file as text, every secret masked
get.description: A string is masked when its key is one `markitai config show` redacts (any key naming an API key, token, secret, password, credential, cookie or authorization, and every string beneath one), or when it is a value of an `extra_http_headers` object, unless it starts with `env:`: it becomes its masked form (`sk…7890`). An `api_base` (or `*_api_base`) loses its userinfo and secret query values. `text` is the file's own text, layout and key order unchanged, with only each masked string literal replaced (`{}` when there is no file; null, with `problem`, when the file is not UTF-8 text, not a JSON object or writes one key twice in one object). `Cache-Control: no-store`.

put.description: Body exactly `{expected_revision, text}` (else 422 `invalid_settings_request`); `text` over 1 MiB or a body over 1.5 MiB: 413 `config_too_large`. Session model/provider overrides active: 409 `settings_read_only`. `expected_revision` not the file's current revision: 409 with `detail` `{code: "stale_revision", current_revision}`. `text` must be a JSON object that writes no key twice in one object (422 `invalid_config`, `line L, column C: …` for a parse error or a repeated key). A masked value sent back unchanged at the position GET sent it is put back in place as the stored literal; a masked value anywhere else is refused (422 `invalid_config`, naming its JSON pointer). The result must be a valid configuration (422 `invalid_config` with the validation message). A `llm.model_list` weight must be a whole number from 0 to 100 (422 `invalid_weight`, naming the entry: `/llm/model_list/N (model in group): …`), unless the file already holds that entry (same `model_info.id`, else group and model) with that same weight. Saved atomically like the other settings changes (409 `config_changed` when the file changed meanwhile; 500 `settings_durability_unknown`); the file is saved exactly as written (the sent text byte for byte, with only the kept masked values put back). The models and providers apply at once; `restart_required` is true when anything else changed, which is read at the next start. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

get.summary: Quick-add candidates from provider keys in the service's environment

post.summary: List a provider's models with the given or saved connection
post.description: A discovery that lists nothing answers 200 with `status: "unavailable"`, a `detail` and a `reason`, as a failed connection test does: a missing key is found before any request is sent.

post.summary: One short request to exactly one deployment

200.description: Test outcome; a provider failure is `ok: false`

get.summary: A user token's own models and the models the admin shares
get.description: Only for a user token; the admin token (and `--no-auth` callers): 403 `user_token_required`. `shared` lists the admin's shared models that are on (admin weight above 0) with only `id`, `model`, `provider`, `weight` (the user's own weight for it, else the admin's; 0 = off for this user only, still listed) and `default_weight` (the admin's): never a key, address or connection. `revision` also covers the user's shared-model weights once it has set one. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

get.summary: The provider cards a user token may connect, then its own connections
get.description: Built-in cards except the providers that sign in with the server's own account or cloud login (subscriptions, Vertex AI, watsonx, GigaChat; Bedrock stays, with a key of the user's own); no environment cards; `key_variable` always null, no `credential`; `default_base` null when the documented address is on the server's machine. Only for a user token (403 `user_token_required`). `Cache-Control: no-store`.

parameters.name: refresh
parameters.description: Accepted for compatibility; the list is computed on every request

get.summary: The editable fields of one of the user's own connections; the key only masked
get.description: As the settings' credentials, over the user's own connections only (any other id: 404 `settings_entry_missing`); `api_key_source` always null. Only for a user token (403 `user_token_required`). `Cache-Control: no-store`.

post.summary: List a provider's models with the given key or one of the user's own connections
post.description: As the settings' discovery, resolved over the user's own connections and models, never with the server's environment credentials. A provider that signs in with the server's own account: 422 `server_credentials`; an address on the server's machine (also a provider's documented local address): 422 `server_address`; `provider_id: "env:…"`: 422 `invalid_settings_request`. Only for a user token (403 `user_token_required`). `Cache-Control: no-store`.

post.summary: One short request to one of the user's own models, a draft, or a shared model
post.description: `{deployment_id}` of one of the user's own models, or a draft `{model, api_key?, api_base?}`; a shared model's id there or any other id: 422 `invalid_settings_request` (`deployment not found`), nothing is sent. `{shared_id}` alone (with any other field: 422 `invalid_settings_request`) tests a model the admin shares and users see (else 422 `invalid_settings_request`, `deployment not found`, nothing sent) on the server, with the admin's key, connection and address; the answer is only `{ok: true, detail: "Model test passed"}` or `{ok: false, reason, detail: "The shared model did not pass its test; ask the admin to check it"}`, never the provider's words, an address or a variable. A user runs one shared-model test at a time and at most 6 per rolling minute; beyond: 429 `provider_busy` with `Retry-After` (seconds), nothing sent. The rules of the user's models apply (`server_credentials`, `key_or_address_required`, `server_address`); literal credentials only, never the server's environment, and no `key_variable` in the answer. Only for a user token (403 `user_token_required`). `Cache-Control: no-store`.

200.description: Test outcome; a provider failure is `ok: false`

post.summary: Atomically add 1–50 models of the user's own
post.description: As the settings' batch, over the user's own lists (credential references name only the user's own connections and models). Every model needs a key of the user's own, or an address of its own (keyless; stored with the placeholder): 422 `key_or_address_required`; a provider that signs in with the server's own account (subscriptions, Vertex AI, watsonx, GigaChat, Bedrock without a key): 422 `server_credentials`; an address on the server's machine (`localhost`, loopback, `0.0.0.0`, `::`, also as a provider's documented address): 422 `server_address`; `credential_provider_id: "env:…"`: 422 `invalid_settings_request`; more than 50 models: 409 `model_limit`. Saved owner-only in `MARKITAI_HOME/serve/user-models/<token id>.json`, never in the configuration file. Only for a user token (403 `user_token_required`). `Cache-Control: no-store`.

patch.summary: Change one of the user's own models
patch.description: As the settings' PATCH, without `share` (422 `invalid_settings_request`), and with the rules of the batch. Only for a user token (403 `user_token_required`). `Cache-Control: no-store`.

delete.summary: Delete one of the user's own models; its connection stays saved

patch.summary: Change one of the user's own connections and every model linked to it

delete.summary: Delete one of the user's own connections and its models

patch.summary: The user's own weight for a model the admin shares
patch.description: Body exactly `{expected_revision, weight}` (`weight` a whole number from 0 to 100 or null, else 422 `invalid_weight`; another key: 422 `invalid_settings_request`; not JSON: 422 `json_required` / `invalid_json`). `{id}` must be a shared model users see now (`SharedModel.id`), else 404 `settings_entry_missing`, nothing saved. A weight equal to the admin's, or null, removes the user's override; 0 turns that shared model off for this user only. Kept in the user's own file as `shared_weights`; the admin's view and routing do not change. Stale `expected_revision`: 409 with `detail` `{code: "stale_revision", current_revision}`. Only for a user token (403 `user_token_required`). `Cache-Control: no-store`.

get.summary: The user's own models file as text, every secret masked
get.description: A document the server writes from the user's lists (not the file's bytes): pretty JSON with two-space indent, LF line breaks and a final line break, keys `models` (its `llm.model_list` entries as stored), `providers` (its connections as stored) and `shared` (`[{id, model, weight}]`, each model the admin shares and users see, with the user's effective weight). Secrets are masked by the rules of `GET /api/settings/config`. `path` null, `origin` `user`, `exists` whether the user's file exists, `revision` the same value as `GET /api/me/models`' `revision`, `problem` null, `read_only` false. Only for a user token (403 `user_token_required`). `Cache-Control: no-store`.

put.summary: Replace the user's own models from its document
put.description: Body exactly `{expected_revision, text}` (else 422 `invalid_settings_request`); limits as `PUT /api/settings/config` (413 `config_too_large`). Stale `expected_revision`: 409 with `detail` `{code: "stale_revision", current_revision}`. Kept masks are put back as `PUT /api/settings/config` does; any other masked value is refused. Then 422 `invalid_config` for text that is not JSON or writes one key twice in one object (`line L, column C: …`), not an object, a top-level key other than `models`, `providers`, `shared`, wrong types, a `shared` id that is not a model the admin shares, or duplicate ids. Absent `models` / `providers` are empty; `shared` entries take `id` and `weight` (a whole number from 0 to 100 or null; `model` and `default_weight` are ignored); a weight outside 0–100 in `shared` or `models` is 422 `invalid_weight` naming the entry (`shared/N (id): …`, `models/N (model): …`) unless it is the one the user already has; a shared model left out, or set to the admin's weight, follows the admin's weight. The rules of the Models routes apply (422 `server_credentials`, `key_or_address_required`, `server_address`, `invalid_settings_request` for `env:` values; 409 `model_limit`); models without `model_info.id` get one; the result must combine into the user's pool (else 422 `invalid_config`). Saved owner-only and atomically in the user's own file; unchanged text writes nothing and keeps the revision. `restart_required` is always false. Only for a user token (403 `user_token_required`). `Cache-Control: no-store`.

bearerAuth.description: The startup token (printed at start, or MARKITAI_SERVE_TOKEN). Required for API clients, including loopback, unless authentication is explicitly disabled. Designated downloads can instead use a single-use ticket.

tokenQuery.name: token
tokenQuery.description: The startup token as a query parameter; accepted for compatibility, but it can end up in logs and history, so prefer the header.

ticketQuery.name: ticket
ticketQuery.description: A single-use download ticket from POST /api/download-tickets, valid for one GET of the path it was issued for within 60 seconds.

SettingsId.name: id
SettingsId.description: A deployment or provider identity from the settings views

UserModelsId.name: id
UserModelsId.description: A deployment or connection identity of the user's own, from its views

PageNumber.name: n
PageNumber.description: 1-based page number; not a whole number: 422 `invalid_page_request`; past the last page: 404 `page_not_found`

ExpectedRevision.name: expected_revision
ExpectedRevision.description: The revision the change was drafted against

UserModels.description: The user's models after the change

detail.description: The service's English message, or an object for settings conflicts that carry `detail.code`

reason.description: Stable machine code of the specific cause. The list is the set the service writes; new codes may be added.

history_retention_days.description: Days a finished job is kept; null when it is kept until deleted

access.description: Who is asking: `admin` (the server token, or a loopback client with --no-auth) or `user` (a user token, with its `label`; an anonymous --no-auth client is a `user` without one)

BuildInfo.description: Which build answers, for every caller

commit.description: The short hash of the commit it was built from; null outside a checkout

built_at.description: When it was built, RFC 3339 UTC (`2026-10-14T09:30:00Z`); null when unknown

dirty.description: The worktree differed from that commit

Features.description: What this service implements beyond the base job API, for a client shared with other backends

url_lists.description: Uploaded `.urls` files expand into URL items

job_labels.description: `label` on POST /api/jobs, echoed in snapshots and history

token_regenerate.description: POST /api/access-token/regenerate; false when the server runs without a token (--no-auth)

user_tokens.description: /api/access-tokens; false when the server runs without a token (--no-auth)

user_models.description: /api/me/models (a user token's own models) and `share` on the admin's models; false when the server runs without a token (--no-auth)

user_config.description: GET and PUT /api/me/config (a user token's Edit config); false when the server runs without a token (--no-auth)

text_only.description: v1.19: `text_only` in job options (images and PDFs: only the recognised text)

CloudflareCapabilities.description: Local prerequisites only: no network request and no cloud permissions verification. Untrusted clients receive a fixed unavailable response.

RemoteProcessingDisclosure.description: At least one accepted attempt requested Cloudflare. This is request scope, not evidence of execution, request count, or actual fees. It survives output rollback and later retries; history summarizes any marked item. Existing pricing and cost_usd cover LLM processing only.

notice.const: Cloudflare requested; external charges not included
notice.description: English fallback; clients should localize using the stable fields.

path.description: `/api/jobs/{job_id}/files/{relpath}`, `/api/jobs/{job_id}/archive`, `/api/jobs/{job_id}/items/{item_id}/archive`, `/api/jobs/{job_id}/items/{item_id}/original/file`, `/api/jobs/{job_id}/items/{item_id}/original/view` or `/api/history/archive`, exactly as it will be requested (percent-encoded ASCII, no query)

url.description: The path with `?ticket=`; open it once

last_used_at.description: Kept in memory only; null until used since the server started

model_count.description: In the list: how many models of its own this user has saved (never what they are)

token.description: `mku_` and 64 lowercase hex characters; shown this once

results.description: One per entry, in request order (jobs, then items)

reason.description: What the single route would answer, when not ok

revision.description: `sha256:` and the hex SHA-256 of the file's bytes; `absent` when there is no file

text.description: The file's own text with every secret string literal masked; `{}` when absent; null when the file is not UTF-8 text or not a JSON object

read_only.description: Session model/provider overrides are active; saving is refused

token.description: The new access token (64 hexadecimal characters)

network_url.description: `http://<this computer's network address>:<port>/#token=<new>` when the server listens on every interface and a network address is found; else null

persistent.description: Always false: the token is kept in memory only, and a restart replaces it

startup_variable.description: `MARKITAI_SERVE_TOKEN` when the startup token came from that variable (a restart takes it again); else null

JobOptions.description: Omitted or null fields use server configuration except Cloudflare defaults, which are disabled unless explicitly selected and confirmed in this request. Confirmation is never inherited from history.

text_only.description: Images and PDFs: write only the recognised text (`output.text_only`); offered when `features.text_only`

strategy.description: auto, static, playwright, defuddle, jina or cloudflare. A job a user token owns (its retries too, whoever asks) is refused a remote one (defuddle, jina, cloudflare) with 403 remote_processing_forbidden, and a remote server default runs as auto for it.

backend.description: cloudflare is refused for a job a user token owns (403 remote_processing_forbidden).

remote_processing.description: Consent for the explicitly selected Cloudflare strategy/backend in this request only. Requires a trusted client and locally ready server; never/hard-off policies win.

stopping.description: Original items that were waiting when the request arrived

options.description: Replaces the item's last options; omitted or null inherits selections but never remote_processing consent. Both retry and enhance reconvert the original source, so Cloudflare must be confirmed for each request.

usage.description: cost_usd, requests, input_tokens, output_tokens and by_model rows with the Pricing counters

options.description: This item's saved repeat selections, falling back to job options for older histories. Always an object; remote_processing and internal metadata are omitted. Snapshot and SSE item responses include it. Enhancement does not change saved repeat selections.

error_code.description: Core conversion code or service cause of a failed item

models.description: The models whose requests produced the retained result, in name order; absent when none did

source_size.description: Bytes of the uploaded original; absent for URLs and CLI records

page_sources.description: A PDF's pages, each with where its text came from; empty for other items and for earlier records

PageSource.description: Where one PDF page's text came from

source.description: text: the text layer; ocr: OCR of the page image; mixed: the text layer with its pictures OCR'd, or a vision model reading the page image beside it

reason.description: A short English note: text layer trusted, no text layer, text layer failed the script check: ..., OCR forced by --ocr ...

RerunFailure.description: Latest failed rerun while the previous successful non-skipped output was retained; independent of observed model usage

label.description: The label the job was submitted with; null when none

download.description: API path of the stored original bytes (also a download ticket path); null when none is kept

view.description: API path of the page for a sandboxed frame (`…/original/view`, also a download ticket path) when `kind` is `html`; else null

pages.description: Page boxes, in order, at most 2000: points of the visible page box after rotation for a PDF, pixels for an image or screenshot; for a URL item's `html` page, its page screenshots when the conversion saved any, else the compare screenshots a browser that loaded the page took (a fallback view; not result files, never sent to a model); else empty for html, text and none

page_count.description: PDF pages, 1 for an image, the number of screenshots (also for a URL item's `html` page that has them), else 0

reason.description: Why `kind` is `none`: no original kept (a CLI-recorded job, a URL page not converted from HTML here, or a removed upload), a format without a browser view and no screenshots, or a PDF or image this build cannot open

page.description: The kept page as a frame without scripts shows it; null when no page is kept

screenshot.description: The page in the browser that took its screenshots, when they were taken; null when none are kept or the job predates the record

capture.description: v1.14, URL items: how usable each kept view was when it was captured; null for an upload. A job without a record (older or Python jobs) has its kept page judged when asked and no screenshot quality.

blocks.description: v1.14: API path of `…/original/blocks` when the item keeps its screenshots' block boxes and `pages` are those screenshots; else null

state.description: `challenge`: a verification, captcha, bot check or login page instead of the content; `empty`: a page that only asks for JavaScript, or under 80 characters of text; else `ok`

text_length.description: Unicode characters of the visible text, white space runs counted as one and the ends trimmed, at most 1 000 000

title.description: The document's title, white space collapsed, at most 200 characters; null when it has none

reason.description: Why it is not `ok`; null when it is

width.description: CSS pixels of the area the screenshots cover

blocks.description: Headings, paragraphs, list items, code, definitions, cells, quotes, captions, tables, pictures, and div/section/article for the words they hold directly; document order, at most 5000, none that starts below `height`

text.description: White space collapsed, at most 2000 characters; a picture's alt text

bbox.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in CSS pixels from the page's top-left corner

width.description: Points; the descriptor's box of this page

bbox.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in points from the page's top-left corner, y growing down

images.description: The boxes the page's pictures are drawn in, in drawing order; absent from a server that does not report them

bbox.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in points from the page's top-left corner, y growing down

truncated.description: The outline has more entries than are listed

markdown_bytes.description: Size of the whole selected Markdown

label.description: The label the job was submitted with; null when none

items.description: With `include=items`: every item as the job snapshot shows it

share.description: An admin's saved model: `shared` when users' conversions may use it (`model_info.share` in the configuration file). Absent on detected rows and on a user's own models

batch_remove.description: The batch route also removes saved deployments (`remove`)

configured.description: The user has models of its own

routable.description: The user's own and the shared models can serve a conversion now

shared.description: The admin's shared models that are on, in the configuration's order

limit.description: Models of its own a user may save

batch_remove.description: The batch route also removes saved deployments (`remove`)

SharedModel.description: A model the admin shares: what it is, never its key, address or connection

id.description: The admin's deployment id: taken only by `PATCH /api/me/models/shared/{id}` and `POST /api/me/models/test` `{shared_id}`

provider.description: `custom` for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, else the model prefix

weight.description: The user's weight for it: its own (`PATCH /api/me/models/shared/{id}`), else the admin's; 0 = off for this user

provider.description: A model prefix (`openai`, `groq`, …) or `custom` for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint

kind.description: `compatible`: a built-in OpenAI-compatible provider beyond the reference's popular list; `common`: any other built-in provider

group.description: The provider picker's group; absent for a provider the catalog does not know

icon.description: Key of the brand mark the workbench draws (its vendored lobehub marks); null for a monogram; absent for a provider the catalog does not know

aliases.description: Further model prefixes routed the same way, then other names the provider is searched by

credential.description: How the connection authenticates when the environment supplies its key: `env:VAR`. On an `environment` card always; on a `configured` card when its key is an `env:VAR` reference, or when it stores no key (a hand-written entry, never the keyless placeholder), may use the environment's credentials and one of its provider's key variables is set; otherwise absent

default_base.description: The provider's documented endpoint; null when every server has its own

key_variable.description: The environment variable read for the key

key_optional.description: No key needs to be entered: a local server, a subscription runtime, or a cloud that reads its own credentials

supports_discovery.description: False when the provider has no model list endpoint: enter model IDs by hand

api_key_masked.description: The saved key masked: the first two and last four characters of a key of 12 or more (`sk…7890`), the last two of a shorter one (`…90`), `…` under four characters; an `env:NAME` reference as it is. An update without `api_key` keeps the saved key; a masked key sent as `api_key` is refused (422).

api_key_source.description: `environment` when no key is saved and the server found one in its environment (a process variable or a dotenv file); `api_key_masked` then names the variable

api_base.description: The saved address with its userinfo and the values of secret query or fragment parameters replaced by `…` (`https://…@host/v1?token=…`); an `env:NAME` reference as it is. Sent back unchanged it keeps the saved address; any other value with `…` is refused (422).

remove.description: Saved deployment ids to remove, as the list at `expected_revision` names them

DeploymentPatch.description: Omitted fields are kept; null clears api_key or api_base.

share.description: The admin's route only: `shared` lets users' conversions use this model, `private` (the default) stops that; may be sent alone with `expected_revision`

UserDeploymentPatch.description: Omitted fields are kept; null clears api_key or api_base.

UserProbeRequest.description: One of the user's own models, a draft model with optional credentials, or `{shared_id}` alone: a model the admin shares.

detail.description: English summary; for a failure its cause, such as `Model discovery returned HTTP 401: <the provider's message>`, `Model discovery timed out`, `Model discovery request failed: <cause>` or `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is not set on the server, so nothing was sent`; never the key

reason.description: Only on a failed discovery (`status: "unavailable"` from a live list or a subscription runtime): why. `no_key`: no key while the provider needs one, found before any request, or a keyless request refused with 401/403; `key_rejected`: HTTP 401 or 403; `rate_limited`: HTTP 429; `network`: no HTTP response (name resolution, connection, TLS, a redirect, which discovery never follows); `timeout`: no answer in time; `provider_error`: anything else, HTTP 404 (the address lists no models) and an unreadable list included. `model_not_found` is listed for symmetry with the connection test and not sent by discovery. A subscription runtime (Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT/Codex) says its cause instead: `runtime_missing` (not found on the server's PATH, or the path variable names no file), `runtime_unsupported` (a release the adapter does not speak; `runtime.installed` names it when known), `not_signed_in`, `runtime_failed` (installed and signed in as far as known, but it failed; `detail` has the adapter's own fixed message), and `timeout`; these come with `runtime` and, except `runtime_failed` and `timeout`, a `next_step`

runtime.description: Only for a subscription runtime that gave no list: which official runtime, the release the adapter speaks and, when it could be asked, the release installed

next_step.description: What to run on the machine where `markitai serve` runs: `install` (a command that installs a release the adapter speaks) or `sign_in` (the login command)

key_variable.description: With `no_key`, the name of the environment variable the key would come from, when one is named; never its value

ProbeRequest.description: Name a saved deployment, or a model with optional credentials.

detail.description: English summary, never a key, a response body or an address with credentials

reason.description: Only when `ok` is false: why the test failed. `no_key`: the deployment has no key and its provider needs one (an unset or empty key variable or `env:` reference), found before any request; `key_rejected`: HTTP 401 or 403; `model_not_found`: HTTP 404 or an unknown-model error; `rate_limited`: HTTP 429 or an exhausted quota or balance; `network`: no HTTP response (name resolution, connection, TLS, a redirect); `timeout`: no answer in time; `provider_error`: anything else

key_variable.description: With `no_key`, the name of the environment variable the key would come from, when one is named; never its value
